# Add managed live track-response subscriptions with captured-state suppression

Parent: #763. Builds on #779 and accepted #783.

**Decision:** ship `subscribeTrackResponse` in both SDKs: one explicitly selected track's live target EQ/input-filter subtotal, with `update`, `readLatest`, `pump`, callback notification and idempotent `close`. Extend the managed lifetime already delivered by #783. This is independently useful to an EQ panel and is the smallest next slice: #779 already owns the capture, evaluator, Worker, membership and actual sample semantics. Keep #763 open. Luna max implements this frozen slice; Astra medium reviews concrete bugs only.

## Requirements first

- A handle selects one existing `TrackResponseQuery` (track, grid, L/R, enforced response bounds) and a bounded notification cadence. Return normalized effective configuration, SDK owner/epoch, job/configuration identity and admitted resource bounds. Resolve and validate the first real capture/result before accepting a new job. A response subscription issues no DSP mutation: report the real `capturedSample`, never rename it `appliedAtSample`. A shared job may return its retained result with that result's original capture sample. No implicit all-track selection.
- Identical effective target/grid/channel/response-bound configurations share one job, one latest result and one capture/evaluation at a time; delivery cadence and callbacks are consumer properties. Different configurations remain separate bounded jobs. A failed subscribe publishes no handle; failed update leaves the old configuration, references and cached result intact. No command batching or new native arm/disarm is needed for these capture-on-request snapshots. Atomic multi-target subscription remains a parent obligation; this child deliberately exposes a single-track request rather than an array it cannot admit atomically.
- Detect **captured response state**, not requested controls. Compare validated sample rate, target mode/meaning, ordered active owner identities/rack/slot/kind/availability/bypass, and both lanes' section ID/kind/enabled/count plus exact rounded coefficient words. The current result exposes both lanes' enable metadata even when its vectors select one lane; comparing the complete owner state avoids stale metadata. Configuration identity separately covers the normalized frequency grid/channels. Use exact bounded equality, not a collision-prone hash. Recompute on first job, captured-state change or configuration change; skip the Worker/native evaluator and publication when state is unchanged. Queued commands do not count as applied changes. A simple bounded capture poll is sufficient for this child; it is not an event feed of every intervening DSP state.
- Give each successful observed state a bigint revision scoped by SDK owner/epoch/job; retain the existing native `snapshotToken` and `capturedSample` alongside it. Name/document that revision as **observed captured-state identity**, not a portable engine coefficient revision or count of all applied edits. A revision advances only after successful evaluation. Unchanged polls must not retimestamp the cached vectors. Count only known publications skipped by a consumer; capture-token deltas cannot count missed states because tokens also advance for unchanged captures and other queries. Intervening uncaptured state transitions are unknown.
- Browser uses the existing owner's bounded off-render timer and one-in-flight gate, respecting each job's fastest consumer cadence and each handle's delivery cadence. Headless uses explicit `pump()` between caller renders and starts no timer or hidden render. Keep one latest result per job and per-handle cursors; `readLatest()` returns owned stable arrays, including protection from a consumer mutating arrays shared with another handle. Callbacks are synchronous notifications, with no payload/promise queue.
- Bound response handles/jobs, retained snapshot/key/vector bytes, points, capture attempts and delivered vector bytes per second before acknowledgement, with concrete configurable defaults. Reuse generated endpoint limits; describe fixed per-engine Worker/Wasm retention separately from per-job storage. Refuse excess rather than allowing request/notification backlogs. Last close releases the job and stops its future capture/evaluation; final managed close stops scheduling. In-flight work has the existing bounded deadline and cannot publish after close/update/session replacement. Reuse the existing engine-owned response Worker; do not create one per subscription. Reload/disposal invalidate every old response handle explicitly.

## Minimum code, at current boundaries

1. Extend `sdk/src/core/observation-subscriptions.ts` with concrete response handle/job state and an optional response-read transport callback. Reuse its owner/epoch, mutation guard, timer, cadence handling and invalidation. Add `subscribeTrackResponse` alongside `subscribeObservations`; keep resident command/binding semantics intact. A concrete second case is enough—no generic scheduler, plugin registry or analysis framework. The timer and headless pump service a bounded selected union serially; there is one response capture/evaluation in flight across jobs and direct response queries.
2. Add an internal “read if captured state changed” operation at the existing query seam. In `sdk/src/browser/engine.ts:501`, retain `trackResponsePending` around capture, comparison and optional Worker evaluation; unchanged captures return before `createTrackResponse`/`client.query`. In `sdk/src/core/live-response.ts:405`, reuse `#run`'s captured bytes/validation and compare before `#analysis`; expose the operation through `sdk/src/core/boundary.ts:574`. Existing one-shot `queryTrackResponse` always evaluates and keeps its behavior. Refactor the existing capture parser just enough to expose a validated exact state key to both adapters; no new DSP math.
3. Wire the optional callback and new entry-point/types through browser/headless exports; extend the existing engine invalidation hooks and SDK examples. The SDK owner receives a bounded capture identity plus an optional newly evaluated result. Reuse the existing live-response and subscription test files and real-browser probe. No Rust, frozen ABI, Worklet protocol or response Worker algorithm change is required.

**Identity trap confirmed in source:** `hosts/host-web/src/ffi.rs:1159` increments `live_token` for every capture. `LiveResponseCaptureSink::new` at `:986` reserves `LIVE_RESPONSE_MAXIMUM_OWNERS` records, but `write_owner` overwrites only active records; unused record bytes can retain previous captures. Therefore neither token equality nor whole-snapshot equality with only time/token removed is valid. Compare the validated active semantic records and their referenced section words, excluding unused storage, offsets and capture-only metadata. `crates/engine/src/realtime/plan.rs:688` explicitly says capture neither drains commands nor advances render. Preserve that behavior.

**Why response before spectrum:** browser response already separates capture from Worker evaluation, and the headless module already evaluates uploaded snapshots. By contrast, `sdk/src/browser/engine.ts:556` owns a one-shot arm/read/cancel sequence, while headless exposes `armSpectrum`/`readSpectrum`; #781 has one preparation-selected target. Repeating that sequence would still lack continuous hops/history/gaps and multi-target capture. It is more code for a weaker claim at this boundary.

## Three discriminating gates, then ship

1. Existing actual headless + three-browser harness: subscribe to a track containing input filters, a named EQ and an excluded dynamic owner; prove independent L/R, owned retained arrays and the same values/membership as #779. Count evaluator/Worker requests: repeated captures with new token/time but identical active words cause zero extra evaluations/notifications; queued control before render does not change state; draining EQ/filter/bypass changes does. Grid changes recompute. Inject altered unused owner slots to prove they are ignored, and altered relevant coefficient/identity words to prove they are detected. Preserve bigint timestamps/revisions above 2^53 through the existing seam.
2. Identical handles share the job; first close preserves it and last close stops capture. Invalid target/grid/budget and refused update retain the old job/results. Different configurations remain independent; resource limits refuse before acknowledgement. Retained arrays survive later polls and another consumer's mutation. Slow delivery keeps one latest publication with honest known skips and no fabricated missed-state count.
3. Delay a capture/evaluation while closing, updating and replacing a same-position session; no stale result attaches to either handle. A throwing callback cannot leak scheduling. Direct one-shot queries and managed polling respect the same one-flight gate. Run proportional SDK type/tests/package checks and the existing actual-browser qualification at one coherent candidate; reuse #779 DSP/realtime evidence because its algorithm/ABI/audio path are unchanged. Root checkpoints, pushes and synchronizes the child after PASS.

## Parent scope remains binding

This closes the selected-track response lifetime and observed-state suppression only. #763 still owns full effect/graph discovery and per-band/per-field selection; atomic multi-target/common analysis service; continuous multi-target spectrum, hop/power smoothing/history/reset/gaps/underrun semantics; portable clock/plan/state/content/publication identities and complete loss/correlation; native/remote provider parity and packed additive vectors/peer compatibility; bounded SAB plus qualified pooled fallback; sample-time joins; integrated examples/resource/realtime evidence and the frozen descriptive transport comparison. It also retains any response integration not claimed here, including a portable state identity and complete effective limits. Staging this child needs no owner rescope. Dropping any binding parent requirement before declaring launch/parent complete does.

## Implementation checkpoints

The first Luna max SDK tranche implements response subscriptions and validated captured-state suppression before evaluation, with unchanged Worker protocol and native artifact. SDK types, deletion policy and focused live-response/subscription tests pass against the accepted #781 artifact (/tmp/issue785-first-focused.log). This is a recoverable working checkpoint, not endpoint acceptance: the response implementation currently has a separate owner/timer; integration into the existing shared managed owner, epoch and serial scheduling remains required by the frozen scope before review.

Checkpoint 1fcc9a25 merges response and resident handling into the existing owner, epoch, mutation guard, poll and timer; adapters instantiate one owner. All 10 focused response/resident/live-response tests pass against the unchanged artifact (/tmp/issue785-common-focused.log), including mixed-service serialization and invalidation. Root identified remaining frozen-contract corrections before acceptance: aggregate delivery-byte admission must include consumer cadence, job identity must include effective request deadline, and polling must honor each response job's fastest consumer cadence. Luna is correcting these with focused tests; this is not final review acceptance. The existing browser probe and SDK usage example are prepared alongside this checkpoint.

SDK candidate 3897a12e8b7b25a16012e80f70c9c18e91a04419 corrects aggregate cadence-weighted delivery admission, effective deadline job identity and per-job timer cadence while keeping headless pumping explicit. All 12 focused tests, all 219 SDK tests and publishable package qualification pass (/tmp/issue785-bounds-focused.log and /tmp/issue785-candidate-{headless,package}.log). Astra medium finds no remaining source blocker; its single attempt-1 verdict awaits the actual browser outcome. The new browser probe required console capacity to issue its tested parameter edit; that fixture setup is corrected without changing SDK behavior.
